chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Five Words that are proclaimed in the Universe
chapter_note: The chapter is extremely fragmentary. Paragraph 1 is a clear hagiographic Q&A frame anchored in contemporary sectarian labels (Baptists, ‘Purified Ones’), while ¶2–¶3 preserve brief internal identifications of the “words” with Manichaean cosmological divinities (Father; Third Ambassador). The identifications themselves stay cosmos→cosmos, but the overall setup likely reflects a later syncretic/interpretive agenda (Mandaean/Elchasaite parallels flagged in the apparatus).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic/dialogue apparatus (“Once again… the disciples… questioned the apostle… Recount to us, our master”) plus explicit anchoring to contemporary groups (“sect of the Baptists… ‘Purified Ones’”). This is editorial framing, not substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] call it by this name is the Father, the l[ife ...] this unnameable, whom no one [...] his name.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite being a continuation of the framed question, the surviving clause itself is an internal cosmological identification (a “word/name” equated with the Father/Life/unnameable). No institutional exhortation or NT citation; reads like a bare teaching equivalence within the Manichaean divine hierarchy.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.45⟩
The second [word is the Thir]d Ambassador [...] of life, whom they also call the father of [...] [...] the first Father.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos equation of a “word” with a named Manichaean entity (Third Ambassador) and related divine epithets. Fragmentary, but the register is classificatory/identificatory rather than pastoral or hagiographic.
